title: Pseudorandom Sequence Period
statementMd:
Polycarpus has recently got interested in sequences of pseudorandom numbers. He learned that many programming languages generate such sequences in a similar way: ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/1505a2bb013efb7ab20b04ab4c345c19fef97ccb.png) (for $*i* ≥ 1$). Here $*a*$, $*b*$, $*m*$ are constants, fixed for the given realization of the pseudorandom numbers generator, $*r*_{0}$ is the so-called $*randseed*$ (this value can be set from the program using functions like `RandSeed(r)` or `srand(n)`), and ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e91a39ad64cd7a33e8f1b67cd60e5b40257de950.png) denotes the operation of taking the remainder of division.

For example, if $*a* = 2, *b* = 6, *m* = 12, *r*_{0} = 11$, the generated sequence will be: $4, 2, 10, 2, 10, 2, 10, 2, 10, 2, 10, ...$.

Polycarpus realized that any such sequence will sooner or later form a cycle, but the cycle may occur not in the beginning, so there exist a preperiod and a period. The example above shows a preperiod equal to 1 and a period equal to 2.

Your task is to find the period of a sequence defined by the given values of $*a*, *b*, *m*$ and $*r*_{0}$. Formally, you have to find such minimum positive integer $*t*$, for which exists such positive integer $*k*$, that for any $*i* ≥ *k*$: $*r*_{*i*} = *r*_{*i* + *t*}$.

## Input

The single line of the input contains four integers $*a*$, $*b*$, $*m*$ and $*r*_{0}$ ($1 ≤ *m* ≤ 10^{5}, 0 ≤ *a*, *b* ≤ 1000, 0 ≤ *r*_{0} < *m*$), separated by single spaces.

## Output

Print a single integer — the period of the sequence.

## Note

The first sample is described above.

In the second sample the sequence is (starting from the first element): $0, 3, 4, 1, 0, 3, 4, 1, 0, ...$

In the third sample the sequence is (starting from the first element): $33, 24, 78, 78, 78, 78, ...$
statementZhMd:
Polycarpus 最近对伪随机数序列产生了兴趣。他了解到，许多编程语言都以类似的方式生成这种序列：![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/1505a2bb013efb7ab20b04ab4c345c19fef97ccb.png)（对于 $*i* ≥ 1$）。其中，$*a*$、$*b*$、$*m*$ 是伪随机数生成器在给定实现中固定的常数，$*r*_{0}$ 是所谓的 $*randseed*$（该值可以通过 `RandSeed(r)` 或 `srand(n)` 等函数在程序中设置），而 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e91a39ad64cd7a33e8f1b67cd60e5b40257de950.png) 表示取除法余数的运算。

例如，当 $*a* = 2, *b* = 6, *m* = 12, *r*_{0} = 11$ 时，生成的序列为：$4, 2, 10, 2, 10, 2, 10, 2, 10, 2, 10, ...$。

Polycarpus 发现，任何这样的序列最终都会形成一个循环，但循环不一定从序列开头开始，因此序列由一个非循环部分和一个循环部分组成。上面的例子中，非循环部分长度为 1，循环部分长度为 2。

你的任务是求出由给定的 $*a*$、$*b*$、$*m*$ 和 $*r*_{0}$ 定义的序列的周期。形式化地说，你需要找到满足以下条件的最小正整数 $*t*$：存在某个正整数 $*k*$，使得对于任意 $*i* ≥ *k*$，都有 $*r*_{*i*} = *r*_{*i* + *t*}$。

## 输入格式

输入仅一行，包含四个整数 $*a*$、$*b*$、$*m*$ 和 $*r*_{0}$（$1 ≤ *m* ≤ 10^{5}, 0 ≤ *a*, *b* ≤ 1000, 0 ≤ *r*_{0} < *m*$），相邻整数之间用单个空格分隔。

## 输出格式

输出一个整数，即该序列的周期。

## 说明

第一个样例即为上文所描述的例子。

第二个样例中的序列（从第一个元素开始）为：$0, 3, 4, 1, 0, 3, 4, 1, 0, ...$。

第三个样例中的序列（从第一个元素开始）为：$33, 24, 78, 78, 78, 78, ...$。
